summary: Masao Abe worked in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Osaka City University, Columbia, Union Theological Seminary, and Kyoto University under Tanabe, Hisamatsu, Nishitani, and D. T. Suzuki. He held professorships at Kyoto, Hanazono, and Nara Universities.

Masao Shizutani specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. He served as an assistant professor at Josai University and at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (attested in 1974).
Masaru Akimoto worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He held a post as professor in the Faculty of Contemporary Society at Kyoto Women's University, attested in 2002 and 2015.

Masashi Nagai is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his education and earned his doctorate at Komazawa University. He spent his academic career at Komazawa University, serving as lecturer, assistant professor, professor emeritus (2017), and president (2019).

Masataka Suzuki works in religious studies, history and archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Keio University (~1968–1978) and held a post there (~1989–2015), later serving as a lecturer at ICPBS and IIBS (attested 2026).

Masataro Sawayanagi studied at the University of Tokyo (~1885–1888). He later held posts at Tokyo University of Education (~1900–1906), Tohoku University (~1911–1913), Kyushu University (~1913–1914), and Taisho University (~1926–1927).

Masato Kobayashi specializes in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1988–1994) and completed his PhD under George Cardona at the University of Pennsylvania (~1995–2000). He was a research fellow at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~2000–2005).

Masatoshi Konishi worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at International Christian University, the University of Calcutta, the University of Tokyo, and Rikkyo University. He was an assistant professor at Hosei University (1971–1984) and professor emeritus at Rikkyo University (1984–2003).

Masatoshi Nagatomi was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Ryukoku University, Kyoto University, and Harvard University, where he completed his PhD under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. In 1958, he became an instructor of Sanskrit at Harvard.

Masayuki Taira works in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1970–1978) and held posts at Kansai University (~1980–1986), Osaka University (~1986–2016), and Kyoto Tachibana University (~2016–2021).

Masayuki Tsukimoto specializes in Japanology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He held lecturer positions at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Massimo Pallottino was a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at Sapienza University of Rome (~1927–1931), later holding posts at the University of Cagliari (~1940–1945) and Sapienza University of Rome (~1947–1980).

Masumi Mochizuki is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He held posts at Minobusan University, serving as lecturer in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (attested 2001), professor (attested 2015), and specially appointed professor (attested 2026).
Mathew Varghese works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He served as a research fellow in 2012 and later as a lecturer (attested 2026) at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Mathieu Beaudouin works in linguistics, Tibetology, and Sinology, earning degrees from Panthéon-Sorbonne University and INALCO. He has held teaching posts at INALCO, EPHE, and Hamilton College, and was appointed a British Academy International Fellow at Cambridge in 2025.

Mathieu Boisvert is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied under Anthony Kennedy Warder and Ravindra Panth. He founded and served as a professor at Université du Québec à Montréal from 1992.
Mathilde Deromps specialized in Indology and linguistics. She studied under Jules Bloch at the École Pratique des Hautes Études between 1911 and 1914.

Mathurin Veyssière de La Croze worked in linguistics, Indology, and history and archaeology. He served as a librarian and antiquary at the Royal Library of Berlin (~1697–1739) and as a librarian at Humboldt University of Berlin (1697).

Matteo Bartoli was a linguist who studied at the University of Vienna, the University of Strasbourg under Heinrich Hübschmann, and the University of Paris. He was an extraordinary professor at the University of Pisa and professor of linguistics at Turin (1908–1946).

Matthew Atmore Sherring was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Coward College (~1845–1850) and University College London (1848–1850) before taking up a post as a missionary with the London Missionary Society in 1852.
